Recent findings suggest that solana is an vital blockchain network in the crypto space, famously known for its low transaction costs, fast processing capabilities, and high transaction throughput. APIs or Application Programming Interfaces, are rules that let 2 different softwares to interact with each other.

Sources indicate that APIs on Solana help developers integrate blockchain functionality into their applications without having to operate or maintain their own RPC infrastructure or validator. Different APIs focus on different needs and factors, so for customers it’s best to choose one that fits their needs depending on the data and performance. Here are our top picks for the best Solana APIs of the month:.

Alchemy is a holistic platform with a wide range of options available for developers. It has JSON-RPC nodes, DAS APIs, and gRPC streaming. The broader developer platform is helpful for developers and teams alike with monitoring capabilities and development tooling options.

According to recent reports, it also has a developer-focused space, which makes it convenient for everyone who wants to manage different blockchain integrations within a broader development ecosystem. Alchemy proves to be a good option for startups and developers who are building with multi-chain applications.

It has been revealed that helius simplifies the process of interpreting and organizing large amounts of raw blockchain information that developers need to go through with its enhanced APIs. The DAS API lets applications retrieve information about digital assets like tokens and NFTs.

The platform also offers webhooks that are useful for applications to keep track of wallet activity. Helius’s broader infrastructure also offers Solana RPC access, historical transaction data, and real-time streaming through LaserStream.

According to recent reports, quickNode’s Solana API supports JSON-RPC API and provides low-latency, Yellowstone-compatible streaming on Mainnet and Devnet. It is built to scale dApps on the Solana blockchain.

Developers can submit transactions, interact with smart contracts, build apps, and read blockchain data. It is especially a great option for developers who are building multi-chain dApps, DeFi platforms, and other enterprise blockchain solutions.

It has been revealed that triton’s API has been designed to help developers build reliable and scalable apps on Solana. It gives them access to the Solana blockchain data with its high-performance RPC endpoints and real-time data streaming services. The infrastructure also supports standard Solana RPC requests, Yellowstone gRPC streaming, and WebSocket subscriptions.

Triton is one of Solana’s original validators and has provided RPC since 2021. Devnet and testnet are provided to developers with every subscription, and JSON-RPC methods are used for reading accounts and tokens.

Dune API is also useful for developers and helps them retrieve, investigate, and analyze Solana transactions, wallet activity, and on-chain events. It translates raw blockchain data into structured information.

It has been revealed that the Execution API on Dune is great for complex historical analysis, aggregated metrics, and querying specific Solana programs. The platform also provides interactive dashboards, real-time data access and analytics for Web3 research.

According to recent reports, chainstack helps developers build, scale and deploy dApps without having to manage complex blockchain nodes. Developers can connect apps to Solana through RPC endpoints and receive real-time blockchain notifications and account updates.

Consumers can also connect apps with standard Solana JSON-RPC methods and provide developer-friendly integrations and have blockchain data access.

APIs on Solana help to make blockchain developments easier and more efficient. Developers can improve the scalability of their projects and access real-time blockchain data. They bridge the gap between blockchain infrastructure and real-world applications and allow developers to focus on making innovative product rather than spending extra time managing data processing.

The analyst wrote the post in Arabic, and according to X's English translation, Binance led the platforms with outflows of approximately 1.439 billion XRP. "The decline in outflows compared with October levels reflects a slower pace of XRP withdrawals from trading platforms, despite continued transfers of large amounts of the cryptocurrency off exchanges," the analyst wrote.

According to recent reports, XRP lost 25.4% in November as of Nov. 22, according to CryptoRank. Before 2026, the token's worst November was in 2019, when it fell 23.3%. XRP also lost 13.8% and 11.8% in November of 2025 and 2022, respectively. In November of 2023 and 2024, the token gained 1.4% and 281.7%.

In 2026, XRP has lost value in seven of 11 months so far, according to CryptoRank data.

Earlier in November, XRP fell to $0.895, its lowest price in two years. On Nov. 23, the token rose as high as $1.026 and then dropped back to around $0.93 the next morning. On Wednesday, it traded at $0.908, down 2.23% over 24 hours, according to CoinMarketCap. XRP's record price is $3.65, which it set on July 18, 2025.

According to Arab Chain, large amounts of XRP continue to move away from the direct trading environment.

"These movements may be linked to holding strategies or the redistribution of assets between wallets," the analyst wrote.

Arab Chain added that continued withdrawals may limit the supply available for immediate sale "if they are not matched by similar inflows.".

"However, these movements cannot be considered conclusive evidence of growing investor confidence or reduced selling pressure," the post reads.

High altitude, bitter cold, zero drivers: autonomous trucks take on Tibetan mine

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Finding qualified equipment operators is hard enough for most mining companies, and the extreme weather, punishing conditions, and oxygen-deprived air of the Tibetan mountains combine to make finding operators even tougher for the operators if this high-altitude copper mine – but SANY thinks they have a solution: fully self-driving haul trucks.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Finding qualified equipment operators is hard enough for most mining companies, and the extreme weather, punishing conditions, and oxygen-deprived air of the Tibetan mountains combine to make finding operators even tougher for the operators if this high-altitude copper mine – but SANY thinks they have a solution: fully self-driving haul trucks.

Chinese equipment brand SANY has deployed fully 60 of its 70-tonne (~80 ton) payload-rated SKT105ED battery electric haul trucks at the Zhibula Copper Mine in Tibet. Operated by Zijin Minig and Tibet Julong Copper, the mine functions at a dizzying 17,700 foot elevation in a region of the Gangdese Mountains known as the Kailas Range, and the conditions there would challenge the health and safety of even the toughest and fittest operators.

It has been revealed that “High-altitude illness becomes increasingly relevant above 2,500 meters,” explains Eacon, in one section of a published paper. “Research involving workers in Andes mines operating between 3,800 and 4,500 meters found that 73% of workers assessed experienced periods of nocturnal oxygen saturation below 85% during their high-altitude shifts, indicating moderate-to-severe hypoxemia.”.

That’s bad news for Zijin’s workers – but the good news here, of course, is that the tech giant won’t be needing many heavy haul drivers going forward.

SANY has been working with Perth, Australia-based Eacon Mining Technology to develop an autonomous haulage solution that uses a full suite of both in-vehicle and ground-based sensors, adaptive vehicle controls, and machine learning that can handle the massive bad trucks even here in the Kailas range.

It has been revealed that “Autonomous haulage offers one way to address this challenge,” continues the Econ report. “Rather than requiring a driver for each truck, autonomous systems allow fleets to be managed through centralized supervision, with personnel overseeing operations and intervening when required. This reduces the need for people to spend entire shifts operating equipment at elevation, while changing how workforce resources are allocated across the mine … depending on the system configuration, some operations can manage autonomous fleets from remote Integrated Operations Centers located away from the mine site, (allowing) personnel to supervise haulage activities from lower-altitude locations, further reducing the need for workers to remain in extreme-altitude environments.”.

The working partnership between the two companies combines SANY’s battery-powered truck platform with Eacon’s full technology stack to create dependable, driverless haul trucks with logic and behaviors that are ideally suited to China’s open-pit mining environments.

Eacon technology is presently operating more than 3,100 autonomous trucks cross more than 40 large-scale mines, including Zijin Mining’s Zijinshan Gold-Copper Mine and at the Norton Gold Fields project in Australia.

In a recent development, while specifications for this specific deployment weren’t disclosed, the SANY SKT105E trucks (the “D” is, presumably, the wide-body variant) the firm has deployed elsewhere are powered by a dual-motor electric drivetrain, pairing two permanent-magnet synchronous motors with a dual three-speed automated manual transmission. The system delivers 570 kW (~765 hp) of continuous power and up to 820 kW (~1,100 hp) at peak output, with each motor producing some 2,430 Nm (~18,00 lb-ft) of peak torque.

It has been revealed that those motors get their electrons from an absolute whopper of a lithium iron phosphate (LFP) battery pack in capacities ranging from 423 to 642 kWh, depending on configuration. The substantial trucks also offer regenerative braking to recover energy on downhill runs, while their fast-charging system can reportedly charge the battery from 20% to 90% in under an hour.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

1Password confirmed a breach on the 25th of November after an attacker copied customer records through compromised backend systems.

It has been revealed that the company said password vaults remained protected, while the stolen information raised the risk of convincing impersonation attempts. For those unaware, 1Password is a password manager that stores passwords, passkeys, and other sensitive information in encrypted digital vaults.

Sources indicate that 1Password began investigating on the 19th of November after an attacker compromised an employee’s corporate GitHub account. The attacker used that access to push malicious code into backend services and download records for some customers.

Those included names, email addresses, account identifiers, creation and sign-in times, and non-secret technical metadata. The attacker also copied public keys, authentication parameters, and tokens from certain invitation, provisioning, and account recovery links.

Sources indicate that 1Password said those tokens alone could not grant access; consumers also needed to complete sign-in or email verification. The attacker also copied private source code and accessed the tech giant’s software deployment systems.

However, it stated that it never stored account passwords or Secret Keys required to decrypt vaults.

It has been revealed that the firm disabled the compromised account and rotated potentially exposed credentials. It reported no internal evidence of account takeovers through exposed provisioning tokens.

The reassurance about vaults left a separate question hanging: how had one employee account enabled such extensive access?

Akash Network founder Greg Osuri noted his trust was “heavily diminished” and called for an option to keep vaults entirely local. Crypto and blockchain CTO Nicki Sanders focused on the intrusion, stating,.

The part that worries me is how they got in.

Trading Strategy co-founder Mikko Ohtamaa favored open-source alternatives, arguing that transparency could make persistent attacks easier to detect.

According to recent reports, others were less categorical. X user Tom Lombardi called the incident,.

The disagreement extended to passwords themselves. Binance co-founder Changpeng Zhao (CZ) urged users to change all passwords.

After 1Password said passwords remained unexposed, CZ acknowledged the clarification and suggested weak-password checks and changing login emails to protect against phishing.

Stolen account details could help scammers impersonate 1Password through convincing recovery messages. That risk already reaches beyond email.

Unit 42 research tracked fake IT-support voice calls targeting over 150 employees across at least ten companies. The activity ran between January and April 2026.

Recent findings suggest that binance’s official risk account previously documented WhatsApp impersonators using supposed P2P account problems to solicit login QR-code scans. Ledger’s campaign tracker documented fake support calls and physical letters directing recipients toward recovery-phrase theft.

  • If XRP gains 5% in a single day, the bullish ETF would target a 15% gain, excluding fees and expenses.
  • If XRP loses 5% in a single day, the bearish ETF would target a 15% gain.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, two proposed U.S. exchange-traded funds would give investors a way to bet on XRP in either direction, with one targeting three times XRP's daily return and the other targeting three times its inverse.

If XRP gains 5% in a single day, the bullish ETF would target a 15% gain, excluding fees and expenses.

If XRP loses 5% in a single day, the bearish ETF would target a 15% gain.

However, investors betting on the wrong direction could lose approximately 15% of their investment in a single day.

The next update is scheduled for Nov. 30. Following a recent amendment submitted to the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), the registration statements for these ETFs are now scheduled to become effective on Monday.

The issuer has repeatedly delayed the effective date. It remains to be seen whether the funds will start trading anytime soon.

The filing covers a total of eight ETFs, including bullish and bearish funds for Bitcoin (BTC), Ethereum (ETH), Solana (SOL) and XRP.

Even if XRP's price remains unchanged over multiple trading days, both ETFs could record negative returns.

Since the ETFs rebalance daily, it's vital to remember that when the price changes direction, the next day's percentage return is calculated based on the investment's value after the previous trading session.

It has been revealed that let's say XRP rises from $2 to $2.20 on Monday and then drops back to $2 on Tuesday. If you hold XRP over these two days, you'll break even.

However, if you invest $100 in the bullish ETF, your position would close Tuesday at approximately $94.55, assuming the fund achieves its daily target and excluding fees and expenses.

If XRP increases by 10% from $2 to $2.20 on Monday, the bullish ETF would target a 30% gain. Your initial $100 investment would now be worth $130.

For XRP to return to $2 on Tuesday, it would need to fall by approximately 9.09%.

The bullish ETF would therefore target a loss of roughly 27.27% on Tuesday. But that loss would be calculated against your $130 position, leaving you with approximately $94.55.

Of course, the bearish ETF wouldn't fare any better.

SWIFT, the largest European financial conglomerate, has just released their latest perspective on quantum computing threats, a topic the crypto community, including the XRP Army, has eagerly debated over the past few months.

The financial community is uniting towards building the post-quantum cryptography (PQC) service, which would replace the algorithms prone to breaking by quantum computing. This aligns with the roadmap of several DLT-based altcoins, including Ripple (XRP) & Algorand (ALGO).

Industry observers note that both of these Distributed Ledger Technology (DLT) based chains are preparing for signatures that erases those threats, potentially fully implementing it by 2028. “Today’s cryptography is deeply embedded across systems, applications & processes”, – the paper states, carving out a transitional path.

Transitioning to new standards requires SWIFT compliant organisations to understand where they are exposed and manage change in a controlled, resilient way. Blockchain adoption comes as a no-brainer: SWIFT’s new ledger acts as a plug between multiple popular chains, including Ripple’s XRP.

Sources indicate that Q-Day is coming. Are we ready?Quantum computing could reshape the foundations of financial security as we know them.Preparing for that future starts now, and it will take the financial community working together.In the latest article in our Perspectives series, Michael… pic.twitter.com/kjLteDKFeM.

Sources indicate that SWIFT’s statement urges companies not to wait for complete inventory of cryptographic assets, but rather prioritise their most critical and exposed systems, beginning the PQC transition. That’s where Algorand (ALGO) & Ripple’s XRP Ledger stands out from the regular crypto crowd. Algorand’s is leading the pack.

Recent findings suggest that the chain’s workable quantum-proof mechanics are being gradually implemented from 2022, targeting broad quantum resilience by the last quarter of 2027. This includes more account features, multisig & solid research into a post-quantum VRF and consensus messaging. First Falcon-protected transfers hit the mainnet in 2025.

It already protects historical state and offers native quantum-resistant accounts that people can use today. On XRP’s part, the Ledger sports a well-documented, institution-oriented initiative with a practical migration path (keeping the same address, dropping the old key) with a mid 2028 goal. However, that’s still pre-development aspirations.

It has been revealed that algorand’s better matched with SWIFT POC aspirations for now. XRP right now uses classical elliptic-curve signatures, known as secp256k1 / Ed25519. No post-quantum signatures are live on the Ledger’s mainnet. The high-standard approach is going to be tested in 2027, while SWIFT is already piloting a roster of Ripple-linked banks.

In a recent development, santander, Standard Chartered, HSBC & Deutsche Bank are the highlights of a double-digit list, but that doesn’t necessarily mean XRP coin is used as collateral or settlement. The chain’s On-Demand Liquidity (ODL) provides an additional liquidity layer via XRP, but it’s optional.

The bigger question is whether XRP can become a standard settlement layer on cross-border corridors.

In a recent development, XRP was about to test the $1 resistance zone, a place it had faced rejection from earlier this week. Can the bulls succeed in reclaiming it as support this time?

In September and October, XRP was oscillating between the $1.30 support zone and the $1.50-$1.55 supply zone. This consolidation gave way to a downtrend that reached a low below $0.90.

Over the past two weeks, the $0.893 and $1.00 levels have emerged as key levels on the daily timeframe for swing traders. A daily session close outside these boundaries will likely decide the direction of the next swing price move.

It has been revealed that at press time, the CMF was at -0.12, signaling heavy selling pressure and capital outflows. The MACD was also moving below the zero line, a sign that downward momentum was prevalent. The MACD line made a bullish crossover above the signal line, an indication of short-term bounce potential.

Despite encouraging ETF flows over the past year, the altcoin’s performance had been lacklustre.

The trend was now firmly bearish, the Directional Movement Index asserted. This indicator’s -DI and ADX readings above 20 confirmed the downtrend, alongside the price structure.

Sources indicate that like the 1-day chart showed a sweep above $1 on Monday, XRP recently made a sweep of the $0.961 local peak in recent hours. Despite the short-term upward momentum, there is a chance of a pullback.

Potential buyers can wait to see the price reaction from the $0.92 and $0.86-$0.88 demand zones.

A bullish reaction on the hourly chart, in the form of something like an engulfing candle, would be a sign that bulls were ready to drive a move toward $1.00.

Industry observers note that traders should be wary of short-term volatility and wait for a positive reaction before buying. Risk-averse traders can remain sidelined until the higher timeframe trend gives a new direction with a move beyond $1.00 or $0.893.

Bitcoin Miners Go 98 Minutes Without Finding a Single Block

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (495 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: U

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that bitcoin miners experienced their longest dry spell since July on Nov.
  • That's the third time in 2026 that miners have gone this long without finding a block.
  • For anyone trying to get Bitcoin transactions confirmed shortly after the previous block, the gap meant waiting more than an hour and a half.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that bitcoin miners experienced their longest dry spell since July on Nov. 26. According to Galaxy's Alex Thorn, it took Bitcoin miners 98 minutes and 19 seconds to find the next block.

That's the third time in 2026 that miners have gone this long without finding a block. The wait ended at 18:28 UTC on Thursday.

For anyone trying to get Bitcoin transactions confirmed shortly after the previous block, the gap meant waiting more than an hour and a half.

Even if you paid a very high transaction fee, you would still have to wait until a miner found the next block before your transaction could receive its first confirmation.

In a recent development, thursday's gap was the 69th longest since 2011, according to Galaxy Research. It was just three minutes shy of the threshold for the top 50.

And this year's other long gap lasted nearly two hours. On July 6, miners took 112 minutes and 26 seconds to find the next block (number 956,953). That was the 19th longest gap on record, according to Galaxy.

Bitcoin automatically adjusts mining difficulty every 2,016 blocks to keep the average block interval at around 10 minutes.

Recent findings suggest that however,  blocks sometimes are found seconds apart. Other times, it takes well over an hour for the next block to be found.

At any given mining difficulty, the chance that a single attempt to find a block will succeed is incredibly small.

If miners have spent 90 minutes trying to find the next block, the chance of succeeding on the next attempt is the same as it was on the first attempt.

Recent findings suggest that so the expected time until the next block is found is still 10 minutes, even if it's already been 90 minutes since the last block was found. That's assuming the network's total computing power and mining difficulty remain unchanged.

Assuming an average block interval of 10 minutes, Thorn said you could expect a gap of at least 98 minutes and 19 seconds about once every 18,600 block intervals.

That means such a gap should occur roughly once every four months, based on an average of about 144 blocks per day.

According to recent reports, galaxy examined 877,290 block intervals going back to Jan. 1, 2011.

Researchers identified 1,948 intervals where at least an hour had passed between the timestamps of successive blocks.

However, Galaxy flagged 97 of those intervals because an adjacent block had a timestamp that was off by at least 10 minutes. This raised questions about the actual length of those gaps.

The longest recorded interval is particularly interesting.

Sources indicate that on Nov. 30, 2011, block 155,290 seemingly marked the end of a 144-minute-and-50-second gap.

However, the miner who found the next block had set its timestamp back by 65 minutes.

After excluding apparent timestamp errors, the longest gap was 141 minutes and one second, recorded on Oct. 13, 2011.

Breaking: Fidelity files for Spot Chainlink ETF as LINK climbs 5.5% – Details

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (376 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Ambcrypto

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent turn of events, Fidelity Investments filed a Form S-1 registration statement with the U.S.
  • According to the 25th November filing, the proposed fund is expected to trade on Nasdaq under the provisional ticker FLNK.
  • At the same time, the fund aims to track the Fidelity Chainlink Reference Rate, which calculates LINK’s price using a volume-weighted median methodology based on data from eligible spot markets.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent turn of events, Fidelity Investments filed a Form S-1 registration statement with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) to launch a spot Chainlink [LINK] exchange-traded product (ETP).

According to the 25th November filing, the proposed fund is expected to trade on Nasdaq under the provisional ticker FLNK. That noted, the fund would also hold LINK tokens directly. This allows investors to gain exposure to LINK through traditional stock market accounts without having to purchase or manage the tokens themselves.

At the same time, the fund aims to track the Fidelity Chainlink Reference Rate, which calculates LINK’s price using a volume-weighted median methodology based on data from eligible spot markets.

Notably, its holdings would be managed by three proposed custodians, including Anchorage Digital Bank, BitGo Bank & Trust, and Coinbase Custody Trust Company.

Recent findings suggest that as expected, this news did have a positive impact on LINK’s price, which was trading at $9.16 at press time after a hike of 5.5% in the past 24 hours. With this, Fidelity becomes the third asset manager to launch a LINK ETF besides Grayscale’s GLNK and Bitwise’s CLNK.

In fact, according to SoSo Value data, GLNK and CLNK have already recorded cumulative net inflows of $128.12 million and $47.88 million, respectively. This in turn has brought their combined cumulative inflows to approximately $176 million. However, neither fund recorded any latest flows on the 25th of November, with both showing $0 in daily net inflows.

Sources indicate that this news comes as the broader cryptocurrency investment products recorded widespread outflows across major digital assets in the month of November. Starting with Bitcoin [BTC] ETFs, which witnessed the largest withdrawals, worth approximately $5.39 billion in net outflows, facing their worst month since launch.

Ethereum [ETH] ETFs too saw $1.30 billion worth of outflows. This was followed by XRP ETFs, which saw $29.18 million in outflows, while Solana [SOL] ETFs registered withdrawals of $57 million. Meanwhile, Dogecoin [DOGE] ETFs recorded relatively smaller outflows of $409,130.

Industry observers note that interestingly, not all products experienced negative flows, as HBAR ETFs attracted approximately $1.71 million in net inflows. This made it the only asset in the sea of ETFs to record positive flows on the day.
